organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and

terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be .  appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in 
any organization of employees or any 
carrier.

dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.

way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10449 at 18 FR 2469 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 24, 1953; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 28, 1953 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3394 to 4127 and 11203 to 11300 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the New York, Chicago & St. Louis Railroad Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the New York, Chicago & St. Louis Railroad Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10449 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board record (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10449_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10449_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_890e74e86f.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a National Mediation Board record for Emergency Board No. 104 stating that no members were appointed and that the parties reached agreement on April 26, 1953, so that no emergency board was set up for hearing the dispute; there is no report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on EO 10449 (a board never constituted is treated like the other emergency-board orders) the order stayed on the books until its express revocation; the fact that the board was never constituted is disclosed here, and the agreement of the parties on April 26, 1953 (a statement in that record) is a spent fact and not an end. The thirty-day report deadline (to May 24, 1953 on the inclusive reading) is a deadline and not an end. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}
